  How to Submit Public Comment:

  Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
  methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

  In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City
  Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the
  Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council.

  Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website or by email as noted
  below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record. Words that would
  disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be read.
  Your comments must be received by 5:00 P.M. on meeting day.

  1. Website: Please submit your comments using our online public comment form at Public Comment.

  2. Email: Please submit your comments via email to cityclerk@sgch.org and include the following on
  the subject line of your email: PUBLIC COMMENT: 03/21/2023 Regular Meeting.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 21, 2023

   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, March 21, 2023

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Wu
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Ding, Vice Mayor Harrington, Council Members Chan, Menchaca,
  Wu

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. COMMUNITY SERVICES EMPLOYEE INTRODUCTIONS
  • Jackie Villalvazo, Recreation Specialist
  • Meyling Suy, Administrative Assistant II

  B. RECOGNITION OF LEI WANG, AD49 WOMAN OF IMPACT HONOREE

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council and Planning Commission Joint Study Session
  Special Meeting of March 2, 2023.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 21, 2023  2
   The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – FEBRUARY 2023

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2022-2023 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 22-30) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2022-2023 Investment Policy. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment report for February 2023.

  D. DIGITAL UPGRADE OF PUBLIC, EDUCATIONAL, AND GOVERNMENTAL
  CHANNEL (PEG CHANNEL) ($5,435 ONE-TIME AND $8,400 ANNUALLY)

  The City broadcasts City Council meetings on the local public, educational, and
  governmental channel (PEG channel). The equipment to perform these
  broadcasts has not been upgraded for many years and currently provides a
  poor quality, analog stream. In order to improve the quality of the broadcast
  services, staff is requesting the City Council approve the installation of
  equipment and subscription for the PEG channel feed. The service agreement
  consists of a one-time equipment installation of cost of $5,435. Additionally,
  there is a monthly subscription cost of $700 per month or annual payment of
  $8,400. Funds are available in the City’s information technology fund to pay for
  these services. The ongoing subscription costs will be paid out of the City’s
  information technology fund.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 21, 2023  3
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the service agreement with
  Spectrum Enterprise/Charter Communications.

  E. APPROVAL OF A PURCHASE ORDER IN THE AMOUNT OF $33,709 FOR THE
  PADILLO ROOM WINDOW REPLACEMENT PROJECT

  The Padillo Room windows are severely rotted and in need of replacement. Staff
  has obtained proposals for a variety of window types and is seeking City Council
  approval to award a contract to provide and install fiberglass replacement
  windows. Based on Staff’s recommendation for the fiberglass option, the costs
  would be $18,708.87. Staff is also recommending the approval of $15,000 in
  contingency funds for the project. The estimated maximum amount of funds
  for the project is $33,708.87. Funds are available in the general fund’s facilities
  contractual account 121-800-07-22-000 of the adopted Fiscal Year 2022-2023
  budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to approve
  a Purchase Order with US Energy Window & Door Incorporated for fiberglass
  windows in the amount not to exceed $18,703.87 plus a $15,000 contingency
  for potential additional work.

  F. AGREEMENT (OPTION 2) WITH LOS ANGELES FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT
  FOR MAINTENANCE OF COUNTY-OWNED STORM WATER CATCH BASINS

  City Council approval is requested to enter into an Agreement (Option 2) with
  the Los Angeles County Flood Control District for the maintenance of county-
  owned storm water catch basins as part of the State Water Resources Control
  Board’s Statewide Trash Amendment. City staff will bill the Los Angeles County
  Flood Control District per the current Catch Basin Cleanout Cost schedule

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 21, 2023  4
   including an annual Consumer Price Index rate as described in Attachment C
  and as specified in the Option 2 Agreement.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  an Agreement (Option 2) with the Los Angeles County Flood Control District
  for catch basin maintenance.

  G. PURCHASE OF A STUMP GRINDER IN THE AMOUNT OF $39,394 FOR THE
  PARKS DIVISION

  Approval is requested from the City Council to purchase a new Vermeer Stump
  Grinder SC382 through a Sourcewell Awarded Contract. The total amount of
  purchase of the Vermeer Stump Grinder is $39,394. The adopted Fiscal Year 22-
  23 Budget includes funding from the Urban Forest Program in account 122-
  800-57-96-512.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Waive formal bidding and authorize the Cooperative Purchase
  Agreement for a Vermeer Stump Grinder SC382, consistent with the
  piggyback bidding requirements pursuant to Municipal Code Section
  34.35; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order with RDO
  Equipment Company in an amount not to exceed $39,394 from the
  Urban Forest Program account 122-800-57-96-512.

  H. ADDITIONAL FUNDING IN THE AMOUNT OF $350,000 FOR THE SEWER
  PUMP STATION PROJECT

  Construction of the Sewer Pump Station is currently in progress and scheduled
  to be completed by April 2023. The original construction cost for this project
  was $845,000 with a $84,500 contingency totaling $929,500. Two unforeseen

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 21, 2023  5
   circumstances have arisen during construction, necessitating an increase of
  $350,000 in the project budget through Council’s adoption of a Resolution.
  There is a balance of $113,559 available in the adopted Fiscal Year 2022-2023
  budget via the Capital Improvement Project 4-20-01 Sewer Pump Station
  Improvements using sewer fund budget account 122-800-38-97-403. The total
  project costs for this item is $1,279,500, which is paid from the sewer fund.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Resolution No. 23-20 to
  appropriate $236,441 from the Sewer Fund to account 122-800-38-97-403; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute a Change Order to increase the Project
  Purchase Order No. 8942 by an additional $236,441 for a total project amount
  of $1,279,500.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. FISCAL YEAR 2022-2023 MID-YEAR BUDGET UPDATE

  The mid-year budget report examines the financial results of the general fund
  through January 31, 2023. The mid-year financial information is analyzed,
  budget projections for both revenues and expenditures are updated, and mid-
  year budget adjustments are proposed. As described in the report, Resolution
  No. 23-16, the mid-year adjustments proposed by departments, will increase
  general fund appropriations by $861,000, the sewer fund by $30,000, the parks
  and recreation activity fund by $29,000, and the Proposition A local return fund
  by $41,000.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the mid-year budget
  update report and adopt Resolution No. 23-16 approving mid-year adjustments

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 21, 2023  6
   to 2022-2023 budget and Resolution No. 23-17 approving mid-year
  departmental staffing adjustments.

  B. ANALYSIS OF EARLY PAYOFF OF THE CITIZENS BUSINESS BANK LOAN AND
  EARLY WITHDRAWAL OF THE 10-YEAR CERTIFICATE OF DEPOSIT

  In December of 2014, the City of San Gabriel borrowed $7.8 million from Citizens
  Business Bank for the construction of the Public Works maintenance facility at
  an interest rate of 1.6%. The City was required to provide 100% collateral for the
  loan in the form of a 10-year certificate of deposit (CD) which earns interest at
  .6%. This report provides an analysis on the financial impacts of an early payoff
  loan and cashing out the CD before maturity.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends the City Council direct staff to move forward with an early
  payoff of the Citizens Business Bank loan and cash out the CD before maturity
  and invest the funds in eligible City investments.

  C. COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

  a.  Recognition of Outgoing Mayor Ding

  b. Selection of Mayor

  c.  Selection of Vice Mayor

  d. New Mayor’s Comments

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 21, 2023  7
   12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, April 4, 2023 at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be

MINUTES OF MARCH 21, 2023

I  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,

  The City Council authorized the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order with

  F. AGREEMENT (OPTION 2) WITH LOS ANGELES FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT
  FOR MAINTENANCE OF COUNTY-OWNED STORM WATER CATCH BASINS

  5. PUBLIC HEARING - None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

I  A. FISCAL VEAR 2022-2023 MID-VEAR BUDGET UPDATE

  Assistant Finance Director Linda Tang made the presentation, noting a correction to
  Resolution No. 23-17 in the third Whereas to read, "Accounting Technician II" instead
  of "Administrative Assistant."

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included clarification that the recommended minimum reserve is 17%
  and the City is at 25.5%; suggestions to make the staff report more understandable
  in the future; Mission Playhouse subsidy amount improvement; fees and rates
  shown in the report are current as of July 1, 2022; revenue and expenditure

  already been expended, though staff is always seeking grants; and appreciation for
  City Manager Lazzaretto and City leadership doing a wonderful job in surpassing
  reserve goals.

I
  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member

  and Resolution No. 23-17 approving mid-year departmental staffing adjustments,
  as amended in the third Whereas to correct" Administrative Assistant" to

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:
